senses.gloss:
Syūma-gṛbh, used of a horse in the Rigveda (vi. 36, 2)
seems to mean ‘grasping the bit between his teeth,’ as a horse
does when anxious to break away from control.

Syūman in one passage of the Rigveda^1 denotes, according to
Roth,^2 the strap fastening the door of a house, the Homeric
ἱμάς, δεσμός.
1) iii. 61, 4.
2) St. Petersburg Dictionary, s.v.

Syūma-raśmi is the name of a protégé of the Aśvins in the
Rigveda.^1
1) i. 112 16; viii. 52, 2. Cf. Ludwig, Translation of the Rigveda, 3, 150, 163.
